In PHP, the final keyword on a method explicitly prevents any subclass from overriding that method.
Private properties are only accessible within the class that declares them, not from subclasses.
In PHP, anonymous classes have generated names that contain a NUL byte, and the portion before that NUL byte is simply 'Class'.

Reassigning a readonly property in PHP 8.1+ throws a TypeError, which is a subclass of Error rather than Exception.
In PHP, an interface can declare constants using the `const` keyword, in addition to declaring method signatures.
The instanceof operator in PHP is used to determine whether a variable holds an object that is an instance of a particular class or interface.
PHP interfaces can declare static methods (supported since PHP 5.5), which must be public and implemented by any class that uses the interface.
In PHP, the instanceof operator checks both class inheritance and interface implementation, so it does not ignore interfaces.
In PHP, interface methods are always abstract and cannot have default implementations; only traits can provide concrete method bodies.
In PHP, abstract methods must be declared as either public or protected, so protected visibility is allowed for abstract methods in an abstract class.
Foo::cases() returns an associative array containing one entry per case in the enum, and this enum has three cases (A, B, C).
In PHP, a trait can declare constants, which can be accessed through any class that uses the trait.

intdiv() throws a DivisionByZeroError when the divisor is zero.

Functions registered via register_shutdown_function() are called during PHP's shutdown phase, which includes when exit() is invoked, causing the script to terminate.

The function takes $x by reference, so modifying $x inside the function modifies $n; 5 + 1 = 6.
In PHP, a foreach by value iterates over a copy (snapshot) of the array, so modifications made to the original array during the loop do not affect the iteration in the same pass.
A static property belongs to the class, not to individual instances, so changes made through one instance are visible through all other instances.
In PHP, a boolean array key is coerced: `true` becomes the integer key `1`, not a boolean key.
Starting in PHP 8.1, a return statement with a value inside a generator function makes that value accessible via the Generator::getReturn() method after the generator is fully iterated.
In PHP, a fully consumed generator can be reset to its beginning by calling rewind() on it, allowing it to be traversed again from the start.
The yield from construct (introduced in PHP 5.5) delegates yielding to another generator or iterable, flattening its values into the enclosing generator.
Calling a generator function g() returns a Generator object, so get_class(g()) returns the class name "Generator".
yield from [1, 2, 3] yields three elements (1, 2, 3), so iterator_to_array produces an array of length 3, and count returns 3.
SplStack implements a LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) stack, while SplQueue implements a FIFO (First-In, First-Out) queue.

ArrayIterator is a PHP class that implements the Iterator interface, allowing you to wrap an existing array and traverse it using iterator methods such as current(), next(), key(), valid(), and rewind().
ArrayObject implements the Iterator interface, so it can be traversed with foreach.
password_hash() automatically generates and embeds a salt in the returned hash string; the function signature does not provide any parameter for passing a custom salt.

password_verify returns true (yes) because the plaintext 'secret' matches its own PASSWORD_DEFAULT hash.

session_regenerate_id() generates a new session ID on login, invalidating any previously set ID and preventing attackers who tried to fix a session ID from gaining access to the user's session.
The php_sapi_name() function returns the name of the SAPI (Server API) currently in use, such as 'cli', 'apache2handler', or 'fpm-fcgi'.
session_destroy() only removes the session data from the server; the session ID cookie in the browser remains and must be separately set to expire or be cleared.
You must explicitly call session_start() before the $_SESSION array is initialized and populated with session data; without it, $_SESSION is not available.

In Clean/Onion architecture, the dependency rule mandates that inner (core/domain) layers depend on nothing outside of themselves, while outer layers may depend inward—dependencies always point toward the center.
In DDD and clean architecture, domain entities are pure PHP objects that must not depend on infrastructure layers like Doctrine or Symfony, importing only the language and standard library.
Controllers and Twig templates belong to the presentation layer, not the business-logic layer, even though they invoke use cases.
In the Onion Architecture, the very center is the pure Business Logic (or Domain), which contains no dependencies on any outer layers.
deptrac and similar tools statically analyze the dependency graph of a PHP project and will fail the build when a forbidden cross-layer call is detected.

A Repository is a component that provides a collection of domain entities/aggregates while abstracting and hiding the underlying storage mechanism (e.g., database) behind a well-defined interface.

In clean architecture, the domain and use cases depend on repository interfaces (abstractions), so only the infrastructure layer—where concrete database adapters live—needs to be swapped when changing PostgreSQL to another database.
An aggregate is a domain concept representing a cluster of entities and value objects bounded by a consistency boundary, not a physical database table.
By definition, a Value Object is immutable and uses value-based equality (comparing field values) rather than identity-based equality.

In DDD, repositories manage the lifecycle of an aggregate through its root, maintaining the aggregate's invariants rather than providing access to individual entities within it.
In Domain-Driven Design, ubiquitous language is the shared terminology that bridges the domain experts' natural language with the code's model vocabulary.
In model theory, the domain (or universe of discourse) is the boundary within which a model consistently interprets a language, while outside it the same symbols can denote objects in other models.
DDD recommends a rich domain model where behavior is encapsulated within domain objects, not an anemic model that pushes all logic into services.

In Domain-Driven Design, a bounded context establishes an independent model boundary where the same term (e.g., 'Customer') can be represented as a different class with its own attributes and behavior in each context, avoiding ambiguity across the system.
Symfony's DI container stores service definitions and only instantiates a service instance when it is first requested via the container, making creation lazy by default.
The symfony route:list console command displays a table of all registered routes in a Symfony application.
Symfony autowiring automatically detects and wires services based on type hints, so you do not need to manually declare every service in services.yaml.
Twig templates are compiled into executable PHP code (a string), not PHP classes; the compiled code is then cached between requests.
In Symfony's dev environment, the container is cached and only rebuilt when tracked files (PHP classes, config files, etc.) have changed, rather than being regenerated on every request.
The SYMFONY_ENV environment variable selects the active Symfony environment (e.g., dev, prod, staging).
Symfony controller methods must be public; the framework's router dispatches to them via public invocation, so private methods cannot be routed to.

PHP's event systems (such as Symfony's) do not give subscribers inherent priority over listeners; priority is determined by the priority parameter of each individual listener, not by how it was registered.
Symfony 6.0 removed the legacy guard security system and uses the new authenticator-based architecture built on AuthenticatorInterface.
The #[IsGranted] attribute in Symfony (Symfony 6.1+) checks whether the user has a given role or permission on a controller method, returning a 403 Forbidden if they do not.

Voters are indeed Symfony's mechanism for making per-object access decisions, and the isGranted('EDIT', $post) call delegates to registered Voter classes to determine whether the current user is granted that permission on that specific resource.

While PHP attributes are the recommended approach in Symfony 7+ for validation constraints, Doctrine annotations are deprecated but still supported (they are removed only in Doctrine ORM 3.0, not yet in the versions that ship with Symfony 7).
Symfony forms automatically include a CSRF token and validate it on submission by default.
In Symfony, form validation is always performed server-side via the FormValidator when the form is processed, regardless of whether HTML5 client-side checks pass.
The Symfony MakerBundle command 'make:form' generates a form type (FormType) class.
Symfony hashes passwords using encoders (BCRYPT, ARGON2, etc.) and stores them in the database; the session only holds a user identifier or token, never the plain-text password.
In modern Symfony (4.3+), configuration is organized in config/packages with one dedicated file per bundle or topic (e.g. framework.yaml, doctrine.yaml).
The common practice is to commit a .env file with safe development defaults while keeping .env.local (with real secrets) git-ignored.
The Symfony command 'debug:container' lists all registered services and their aliases in the service container.
The Symfony container exposes a setParameter() method that, in a non-frozen (development) container, can be called from anywhere including a controller to modify a parameter at runtime.
In Symfony, services are private by default; you must explicitly set public: true in a service definition to make them directly fetchable from the container.
Configuration is not mandatory for every bundle; many bundles work fine with their default settings without any config file in config/packages/.
In Symfony services.yaml the correct syntax is %%env(VAR)%% (double percent signs) because a single % is a YAML directive character and must be escaped.
In Symfony, the DEBUG environment variable (e.g., DEBUG=1) enables debug mode, which activates the profiler and Twig debug features.
A message in Symfony Messenger can have multiple handlers configured for the same message class, and they will all be invoked.
The sync transport processes the message immediately in the current process rather than leaving it queued for a separate worker to pick up.
The messenger:consume command starts a Symfony Messenger worker that processes queued messages.
The retry_strategy option (with settings like max_attempts and interval) is defined in the transport configuration of Symfony Messenger, meaning each transport can have its own retry behavior.
Symfony Messenger uses JSON as its default serializer for serializing messages.
Symfony Scheduler dispatches messages through the Messenger component when scheduled tasks are due, which are then handled by subscribers to perform the actual work.
Symfony's database Messenger transport persists messages into database tables using Doctrine ORM.
Symfony's Messenger middleware pipeline is extensible, allowing you to register custom middleware and position them before or after the built-in middleware in the chain.
Symfony follows a release cycle where major versions (e.g., 6.0, 7.0) appear roughly every two years and point releases appear every six months in May and November.
Symfony 8 requires PHP 8.3 or higher as its minimum supported PHP version.
Symfony 7.0 removed support for docblock annotations (such as @Route and validation constraints), requiring attributes as the sole mechanism.
AssetMapper is a PHP-based asset management tool that handles CSS/JS loading through an importmap.php file, eliminating the need for Node.js or webpack.
Symfony follows a single support policy for all versions (4 months of bug fixes + 8 months of security fixes), so 6.4 is a regular release with no separate long-term support track.
In Symfony, when you move to a new major version, the features that were deprecated in the previous major version are actually removed, not kept with warnings.
Symfony provides an UPGRADE guide (e.g., UPGRADE-5.0.md) for every major version release in its documentation repository.

The Symfony asset-packager component provides asset fingerprinting and versioning without requiring Node.js or webpack, and it works alongside the importmap package to replace the webpack-encore workflow.

The next Symfony minor version after 8.1 is 8.2, following Symfony's incremental versioning scheme.

In semantic versioning, 8.2 is a minor release, not a major one (major releases are denoted as 8.0, 9.0, etc.), and Symfony major versions generally deprecate and remove APIs rather than require complete rewrites.
PHP follows semantic versioning, so minor version bumps (8.1 → 8.2) are backwards compatible and do not require code changes.
Symfony follows a pattern of releasing minor versions 0 through 5 per major branch, so the last 8.x minor before Symfony 9.0 is 8.5.
Symfony 8.x point releases maintain the minimum PHP requirement of the 8.0 major release (PHP 8.1+), not PHP 8.5.
Symfony's deprecation policy removes deprecations two major versions after introduction, so deprecations added in 8.x remain available through 9.0 and are removed in 10.0.

Twig's {{ }} block is a templating expression language that does not execute arbitrary PHP code; only Twig-specific syntax (variables, registered functions/filters, property access, arithmetic, etc.) is permitted, not raw PHP constructs.
By default, Twig uses the 'html' escape strategy, which automatically escapes variables when they are output in templates.
The Twig |e filter (also written as |escape) escapes a string for safe HTML output by default, protecting against XSS by encoding special characters.
The intl_numberformat filter in the twig/intl-extra package formats a number according to a specific locale.
The |raw filter outputs a value without applying HTML escaping, effectively disabling auto-escaping for that value.
In Twig, {{ }} outputs the result of an expression, while {% %} is used for control structures like if, for, and set tags.
Twig does allow you to declare variables inside a template using the `set` tag (e.g., {% set myVar = 'hello' %}), as well as through loop variables, the `with` tag, and other built-in variables.
The Twig `dump()` function displays the debug structure of a variable such as an array or object.

Bootstrap is a front-end library providing reusable UI components via CSS, JavaScript, and Sass; it does not handle client-side routing or application state management, which are hallmarks of SPA frameworks like React or Angular.
The .container class in Bootstrap is a responsive, centered container that has a fixed max-width at each breakpoint (e.g., 540px, 720px, 960px, 1200px in Bootstrap 4/5).
The Bootstrap grid splits a row into 12 columns, not 16, and modern Bootstrap (v4+) is built on CSS Flexbox rather than CSS floats.
Bootstrap 5 defines five named breakpoints: sm (576px), md (768px), lg (992px), xl (1200px), and xxl (1400px).
In Tailwind CSS, spacing utilities like .mt-3 or .px-2 are generated by multiplying the numeric suffix by the $spacer variable, so the resulting value is indeed a multiple of $spacer.
In Bootstrap 5, the data-bs-toggle data attribute is the one that enables interactive components such as dropdowns, modals, and offcanss on an element.
Bootstrap 5 removed its jQuery dependency and uses vanilla JavaScript (along with Popper.js) for its interactive components.
Bootstrap dark mode is enabled using a data attribute (e.g., data-bs-theme="dark" in Bootstrap 5 or data-theme="dark" in Bootstrap 4), not a .dark class on the root element.
Doctrine ORM does not create tables at runtime; you must explicitly run schema commands like 'doctrine orm:schema-create' or use migrations to create or alter the database schema.
The persist() method of Doctrine's EntityManager marks a new object as managed (pending insertion) without issuing any SQL until flush() is called.
Doctrine ORM 3's EntityManager::merge() exists and attaches (makes managed) the passed object, returning a managed instance.
DQL (Domain Query Language) in Doctrine ORM is an object-oriented query language that references entity class names and property names rather than raw database table names and column names.
In PHP repository patterns, the find() method returns null when no matching record exists.
DoctrineBundle does not automatically call flush(); you must explicitly call $em->flush() (or use the flush option in forms) after modifying entities.

In Doctrine ORM, once an entity is in the managed (persistent) state, the Unit of Work detects property modifications automatically, so flush() alone is sufficient to commit those changes to the database.
In Doctrine ORM, remove() only marks the entity for deletion in the Unit of Work; the actual SQL DELETE is not executed until flush() is called.

The EXPLAIN command displays a query's execution plan without actually executing the query.

By default in PostgreSQL, a UNIQUE constraint allows multiple rows with NULL values because NULL is not considered equal to any other value, including NULL itself.
PostgreSQL's string_agg(expression, separator) aggregate function concatenates string values together using the specified separator.
Plain VACUUM only marks space as reusable within the table; VACUUM FULL is what actually returns freed space to the operating system by rewriting the table.
In a window function's OVER clause, the PARTITION BY keyword divides the rows into groups (partitions) over which the window function is computed.

READ COMMITTED only protects against dirty reads; a subsequent read within the same transaction can still see different values after another transaction commits an update, which is a non-repeatable read.

PostgreSQL's default autocommit behavior wraps each individual SQL statement in its own implicit transaction that is committed automatically unless you explicitly start a multi-statement transaction with BEGIN.
The COMMIT statement finalizes a transaction by persisting all changes made within it to the database.

Indexes accelerate any statement (SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE) that uses a WHERE clause searching on an indexed column, because the index helps the engine locate the matching rows without a full table scan.
PostgreSQL uses SAVEPOINT to create a checkpoint, and ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT to roll back only the statements executed after that point, leaving earlier statements in the transaction intact.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually executes the query to collect real timing and row-count data, whereas plain EXPLAIN shows the plan without executing it.
pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds a vector data type and supports indexing (GIN/GiST) for vector similarity and embedding search.
A partial index (conditional index) includes only the rows for which the specified WHERE condition is true, storing index entries only for those matching rows.

PostgreSQL implements SERIALIZABLE through MVCC snapshots with conflict detection at commit time (detecting anomalies like write-skew), not by taking row locks on read; it uses snapshot reads without read locks.
HTTP status 201 'Created' indicates that the request successfully created a new resource.
HTTP 204 No Content indicates a successful request with no response body, and is commonly returned after a DELETE operation.
Per the HTTP specification (RFC 7231 §4.1), DELETE is idempotent because repeating the request has no additional effect beyond the initial deletion of the resource.
The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is sent by the server (in its response), not by the client.
HTTP status 429 (Too Many Requests) is specifically defined in RFC 6585 for indicating that a client has sent too many requests in a given period, meaning they've exceeded a rate limit.
The statement is backwards: 4xx codes indicate client errors, and 5xx codes indicate server errors.
The Content-Type header specifies the MIME type of the request or response body.
RFC 5789 explicitly states that PATCH is not required to be idempotent, whereas PUT is always idempotent per RFC 2616/7231.
You should use hash_equals() instead of ==, because hash_equals() performs a constant-time comparison, mitigating timing attacks, while == is subject to type juggling and is not constant-time.
CSRF tokens are server-generated, typically tied to the session, and validated by the server on state-changing (unsafe) requests to prevent cross-site request forgery.
The Content-Security-Policy HTTP header is used by web browsers to implement Content Security Policy, which helps protect against XSS and data injection attacks.
OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework, not an authentication protocol; the access token grants permission to access resources rather than primarily identifying the user.
XSS is prevented by context-aware output encoding when rendering data on a page, not by input validation before storage.

In the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, the authorization server redirects the user back to the redirect_uri with an authorization code parameter, which the client then exchanges at the token endpoint for an access token.
